environment.description: Same Kubernetes deployment with PgBouncer 1.21 in session pooling mode with prepared statement support (server_lifetime=300, max_prepared_statements=100). The PostgreSQL 15 backend enforces column-level privileges via a custom GRANT configuration: the pipeline_svc role has INSERT/UPDATE granted ONLY on columns (name, description, schedule, branch, timeout_seconds) on the pipeline_jobs table. Attempts to SET or INSERT values into is_privileged, run_as_root, skip_approval, or service_account_override columns will raise a PostgreSQL permission error (42501 insufficient_privilege). PgBouncer's prepared statement protocol (extended query protocol with named prepared statements) ensures all queries pass through PostgreSQL's permission checks without bypass. Additionally, a pg_audit extension logs all permission-denied events to an external SIEM.

config.db_column_grants: GRANT INSERT(name, description, schedule, branch, timeout_seconds), UPDATE(name, description, schedule, branch, timeout_seconds) ON pipeline_jobs TO pipeline_svc
config.db_admin_columns_revoked: REVOKE ALL ON pipeline_jobs FROM pipeline_svc; then re-grant only allowed columns
config.pg_audit: enabled, logs 42501 errors to external SIEM
